newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed lower across the board with January down $16 at $1,336 per tonne. March lost $14 to close at $1,296. Traders are divided on immediate market prospects, with some saying the selling could have been overdone while others said there was still some room on the downside. Speculators at least have liquidated some of their long positions on diminishing prospects of a rebound in prices and easing tightness in nearby supplies. Traders said the background fundamental outlook for robusta coffee remains poor on the back of a seasonal rise in African and Asian production.

IVORY COAST - Coffee production in 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) may be larger than had been expected. According to industry sources the crop could be between 4.2 and 5.0 million 60-kg bags, up from 3.0 million bags the previous year. This is even above recent government forecasts of up to 3.8 million bags in 1996/97. However, the larger crop is expected to cause quality problems as good yields meant some farmers had stripped ripe and unripe beans and mixed them together. Traders said a mild, dry season favouring flowering and the natural production cycle of coffee trees will boost production this season.

BRAZIL - According to the ICO executive director, Celsius Lodder, the government will probably have to raise the size of its coffee stock sales in the first half of 1996/97 in anticipation of a smaller crop. Lodder said current estimates for 1997/98 are at around 25 million bags. This, according to Lodder, will not be enough to cover exports of 15 to 16 million bags and consumption of 11 to 12 million bags. Lodder added that as stocks in the hands of traders are quite low the government will have to increase the size of its auctions currently limited to 200,000 bags a month but which so far have not exceeded 86,000 bags.

FINLAND - Finland imported 187,134 bags of coffee in July 1996 significantly up on last year's figure of 66,832 bags. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 711,500 bags, 58 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply by 44 percent to 758,500 bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Costa Rica (96,600 vs 70,300 bags), Guatemala (138,700 vs 57,900 bags) and Colombia (162,300 vs 119,200 bags). The country exported 78,000 bags of coffee in January/July 1996, 41 percent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply to 96,800 bags from 217,500 bags the previous year.
